lead: Olathe plumbing deals with cold winters, clay soil, basements and fast growth. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers across Olathe.
risk: sump pump failures, frozen pipes and water heater replacement
risk_short: sump pumps, frozen pipes and water heaters
why: Original Town Olathe has homes from the 1900s to the 1950s with galvanized supply lines. Most of the city was built after 1980, and nearly every home has a basement with a sump pump.
Winters freeze pipes near exterior walls and hose bibs. Clay soil moves with the seasons and stresses foundations and sewer lines.
water: Olathe treats water from the Kansas River and Hillsdale Lake. It is moderately hard.
tips: Add a battery backup to your sump pump.
Scope the sewer line before buying an older home.
areas: PipeMend works in Original Town, Cedar Creek, Forest View, Prairie Center, Arbor Creek, Heritage and every other Olathe neighborhood.
permits: Plumbing permits come from the City of Olathe Building Codes Division, and plumbers are licensed through the Johnson County Contractor Licensing program. Kansas has no statewide plumber license.

faq.a: Kansas has no statewide plumber license. Olathe uses Johnson County's Contractor Licensing program, as do most cities in the county. Ask for the license number before work starts.
